FAQs

Frequently Asked Questions

Speaking and Events

What kinds of events can I invite you to?

I speak at churches and universities as well as at conferences, retreats, and community gatherings. I’m available for a single talk or a series of sessions built around a theme your group wants to explore.

What topics do you speak about?

I speak about the New Testament and the ancient world in which it was written. One of my main interests is how Scripture speaks to questions of ancestry and belonging. For example, I can lead a session on what the story of Timothy in Acts reveals about multiethnic identity in the early church and what it might mean for churches today.

Can you tailor a talk or workshop to our group?

Yes. A Sunday school class and a university seminar may be interested in the same passage but bring different questions to it. Tell me a little about your group and what you hope people will take away. We can plan a single session or a half-day or full-day workshop.

Do you lead guided book studies?

Yes. I offer guided studies of Mixed Identities and the People of God. We can discuss how the book’s New Testament examples relate to your community’s own questions about ethnicity and belonging.

Can you help with a writers’ retreat or a writing day?

If you’re planning a gathering for Christian writers, I’d be glad to hear what you have in mind. We can discuss whether a short talk on writing for a particular audience or a guided session where participants give each other feedback would serve your group.

How do we ask about availability and speaking fees?

Send me a brief note with your proposed date and a little about the event. Let me know where it will take place or if it’s online, and what you’d like me to contribute. We can discuss availability and fees once I have a sense of what you’re planning.

Editing and Publishing

Who do you work with?

I work with aspiring Christian authors who are developing their first book as well as experienced writers who want help with a new project. My background in biblical studies and publishing is especially helpful if you’re writing about Scripture or theology for a general audience.

Can I work with you if I haven’t finished my manuscript?

Yes. If you have an idea for a book, we can talk through who it’s for and what you want readers to gain from it. If you already have a few chapters, I can help you see what’s working and decide where to focus as you draft the rest.

What’s the difference between developmental editing, line editing, and copyediting?

Developmental editing looks at the big picture. Do the chapters build on one another? Does the manuscript deliver what it promises readers? Line editing works at the sentence and paragraph level to improve clarity and flow while preserving your voice. Copyediting addresses grammar and punctuation and checks for consistency in details such as spelling and capitalization.

What if I’m unsure which kind of editing I need?

Tell me what you’re writing and where you feel stuck. If the chapters read well on their own but feel disconnected as a book, for example, we might begin with the structure. A short sample can help us decide where to start.

Can you help me think through how I use Scripture in my writing?

Yes. I can help you consider whether a passage supports the point you’re making and how much biblical or historical context your readers need to follow your interpretation.

What does publishing consulting include?

We can talk through traditional publishing and self-publishing in light of your goals. If you’re pursuing a traditional book deal, I can explain what goes into a proposal or give you feedback on one you’ve already drafted.

How much does editing cost, and how long does it take?

That depends on the length of your manuscript and the kind of editing it needs. You’ll find starting rates on my Work With Me page. Include your approximate word count and any deadline when you reach out so we can discuss a quote and timeline.

How do I get started?

Send me a short description of what you’re writing and where you are in the process. If there’s a particular question or challenge you’d like help with, tell me about it. A few sentences are plenty for a first message.
